title: Microsoft Purview DLP: restrict access to Fabric semantic models and lakehouses
summary: The briefing passes: its opt-in default, licensing, rollout dates and documented restrictions are supported. Minor corrections should restore omitted wizard headings and explain the narrower capacity wording in the PowerShell reference.

claims.claim: This roadmap change adds a DLP restrict access action for Fabric semantic models and lakehouses.
claims.quote: DLP restrict access action allows you to block access to guest users or all users depending on what labels or sensitive information types matches your semantic models or lakehouses.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The action can block guests or all users based on matching labels or sensitive information types.
claims.quote: DLP restrict access action allows you to block access to guest users or all users depending on what labels or sensitive information types matches your semantic models or lakehouses.

claims.claim: DLP already supported auditing and Policy Tip notifications for these Fabric items.
claims.quote: This is in addition to the ability already supported by DLP policies to audit and notify users via Policy Tips based on sensitive content within Fabric semantic models and lakehouses.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: restrictions require a security or compliance administrator to add the action to a policy.
claims.quote: If you would like to start restricting access to internal users or data owners, your security or compliance admin will need to update or create new DLP policies for Fabric to include the new Restrict access action.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining administrator licence prerequisites with consumption billing.
claims.quote: The pay-as-you-go billing model builds on the per-user licensing model. The two are complementary, not mutually exclusive.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The configuring admin account must have Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance, or Purview capacities.
claims.quote:
The admin account that sets up the DLP rules must be assigned one of the following licenses:
- Microsoft 365 E5
- Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance
- Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance
- Purview capacities

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: DLP evaluation workloads affect capacity consumption.
claims.quote: DLP evaluation workloads impact capacity consumption. For information about how this consumption is metered and billed, see Learn about Microsoft Purview billing models.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The printed Purview creation path reaches the restrict access section through the Custom policy and advanced-rule choices.
claims.quote: The Define policy settings page appears. Choose Create or customize advanced DLP rules to begin defining your policy.
claims.fix: Restore the pass-through wizard headings in both copies of this path: Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Assign admin units > Fabric and Power BI workspaces > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > Actions > Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations. Retain the note explaining the Block users selection.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with Name, Policy, ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name=...} and BlockAccess $true creates a sensitive-information rule that blocks matching source items.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name "SocialSecurityRule" -Policy "USFinancialChecks" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name="U.S. Social Security Number (SSN)"} -BlockAccess $True

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The Purview Custom policy wizard reaches Fabric and Power BI workspaces and its Edit control for inclusion or exclusion.
claims.quote: To specify specific workspaces for inclusion or exclusion, select Edit.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -PowerBIDlpLocation All -PowerBIDlpLocationException <workspaceID> -Mode Enable creates an enabled policy excluding the specified workspace.
claims.quote: This example creates a DLP policy named PowerBIPolicy for all qualifying Power BI workspaces (that is, those hosted on Premium Gen2 capacities) except for the specified workspaces.
claims.fix: Append to the workspace-scope row's note: 'The PowerShell reference limits -PowerBIDlpLocation and -PowerBIDlpLocationException to workspaces hosted in Premium Gen2 capacities; the Fabric configuration page instead says Fabric or Premium capacities.' Retain the existing test-tenant caveat and the existing call.

claims.claim: After Custom policy, the wizard asks for a policy name and description before Next.
claims.quote: Name the policy and provide a meaningful description. When done, select Next.

claims.claim: Administrators should pass Assign admin units by selecting Next without assigning units.
claims.quote: Select Next when you get to the Assign admin units page. Admin units are not supported for DLP in Fabric and Power BI.

claims.claim: The restrict access section offers a Block users option followed by a choice of everyone or only outsiders.
claims.quote: select Block users from receiving email, or accessing shared SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams files, and Power BI items. Then choose whether to block everyone or only people outside your organization.

claims.claim: The overview describes retaining access for data owners or organisation members, depending on configuration, and removing it for other users.
claims.quote: the policy restricts access to the data owners or to members of the organization, depending on the policy configuration. All other users lose access to the item.

claims.claim: The troubleshooting page describes the all-users case as blocking everyone except workspace admins.
claims.quote: All users in the tenant: When applied to this group, DLP policies block all users except workspace admins, who can troubleshoot and fix the data, where relevant.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: UserType Member is treated as internal even when the user signs in with an external account.
claims.quote: a member of the organization means a user with UserType = Member. This includes users who sign in with an external account. Because their UserType is Member, they’re treated as internal users.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: UserType Guest users are external and are targeted by Block only people outside your organization.
claims.quote: users with UserType = Guest are considered external. The Block only people outside your organization setting applies to these Guest users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Semantic-model DLP evaluation is skipped when service principal authentication initiates publishing, republishing or refreshing.
claims.quote:
DLP evaluation of the semantic model doesn't occur if either of the following is true:
- An account using service principal authentication initiates the event (publish, republish, on-demand refresh, scheduled refresh).

claims.claim: Semantic-model DLP evaluation is skipped when the model owner is a service principal.
claims.quote:
DLP evaluation of the semantic model doesn't occur if either of the following is true:
... The semantic model owner is a service principal.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: DirectQuery semantic models are unsupported for Fabric DLP.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported for sample semantic models, streaming datasets, or semantic models that connect to their data source via DirectQuery or live connection.

claims.claim: Live-connection semantic models are unsupported for Fabric DLP.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported for sample semantic models, streaming datasets, or semantic models that connect to their data source via DirectQuery or live connection.

claims.claim: Fabric DLP applies only to data in tables stored in Delta format.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric apply only on data in tables stored in Delta format.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Advanced classifiers, including exact data match and trainable classifiers, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Advanced classifiers, such as exact data match (EDM), trainable classifiers, credential classifiers, and named entities aren't supported by DLP for Fabric.

claims.claim: An advanced classifier produces no results even when matching data is present.
claims.quote: If you select an advanced classifier in the condition of a policy, the policy returns no results even if the item contains data that satisfies the advanced classifier.

claims.claim: Other classifiers in the same policy can still return results.
claims.quote: Other classifiers specified in the policy return results if any.

claims.claim: Publishing a semantic model triggers DLP evaluation, subject to the stated service-principal exceptions.
claims.quote:
DLP policies evaluate a semantic model whenever one of the following events occurs:
- Publish

claims.claim: Republishing a semantic model triggers DLP evaluation, subject to the stated service-principal exceptions.
claims.quote:
DLP policies evaluate a semantic model whenever one of the following events occurs:
- Publish
- Republish

claims.claim: On-demand and scheduled semantic-model refreshes trigger DLP evaluation, subject to the stated service-principal exceptions.
claims.quote:
DLP policies evaluate a semantic model whenever one of the following events occurs:
- Publish
- Republish
- On-demand refresh
- Scheduled refresh

claims.claim: Lakehouses and other Fabric items are evaluated when their data changes.
claims.quote: DLP policies evaluate a Fabric item, such as a lakehouse, SQL database, or Mirrored database, when the data within it changes.

claims.quote: The selection of response options they have depends on the choices you make in the User overrides section.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Fabric documentation limits DLP policies and actions to workspaces on Fabric or Premium capacities.
claims.quote: DLP policies apply to workspaces. Only workspaces hosted in Fabric or Premium capacities are supported.

claims.claim: Onboarding a new tenant to DLP can take a few hours.
claims.quote: Onboarding a new tenant to DLP can take a few hours, depending on the number of supported workspaces that are being onboarded.

claims.claim: The Fabric configuration page does not name a licence for restricted users.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Fabric DLP restricted users licensing E5 admin account license required'; opened data-loss-prevention-configure and data-loss-prevention-overview. The configuration prerequisites name the admin account, not restricted users.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Fabric is covered by Purview pay-as-you-go, an Azure-billed consumption model, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Asset billing charges for each day a policy covers an asset.
claims.quote: You're charged for each day that a policy covers an asset.

claims.claim: An asset in an in-scope location counts even if it does not match policy conditions.
claims.quote: The asset doesn't have to match a policy's conditions to be counted, it just has to be in a location that's in the scope of a policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft's example counts 250 assets when a policy covers five of ten Fabric workspaces containing 50 assets each.
claims.quote: A tenant has 10 Fabric workspaces, each with 50 assets. The policy only applies to five of these Fabric workspaces. The asset count for this policy is 250.

claims.claim: The cited configuration, overview and billing-model pages quote no Fabric DLP monetary rate.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview Fabric DLP restrict access pricing additional charge rate asset'; read data-loss-prevention-configure, data-loss-prevention-overview and purview-billing-models. They name prerequisites and counting, not a monetary rate.

claims.claim: A separate charge specifically for the restrict access action beyond asset counting is not published in the material found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft Purview Fabric DLP restrict access pricing additional charge rate asset' and 'site:azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview Fabric "Data Loss Prevention" "restrict"'; read purview-billing-models and Fabric DLP pages; no action-specific charge found.

claims.claim: Excluding workspaces changes which assets the policy covers.
claims.quote: Assets are counted based on the number of items that are in the scope of a policy.

claims.claim: Fabric DLP is not supported in China North.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported in the China North region.

claims.claim: Supported item types include semantic models, lakehouses, warehouses, KQL databases, mirrored databases, SQL databases and Cosmos databases.
claims.quote:
DLP policies for Fabric and Power BI currently support the following item types.
- Semantic models
- Lakehouses
- Warehouses
- KQL databases
- Mirrored databases
- SQL databases
- Cosmos databases

claims.claim: DLP policies apply at workspace scope.
claims.quote: DLP policies apply to workspaces.

claims.claim: Sample semantic models are unsupported.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported for sample semantic models, streaming datasets, or semantic models that connect to their data source via DirectQuery or live connection.

claims.claim: Streaming datasets are unsupported.
claims.quote: DLP policies for Fabric aren't supported for sample semantic models, streaming datasets, or semantic models that connect to their data source via DirectQuery or live connection.

claims.claim: Policy creators must belong to Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin or Security administrator role groups.
claims.quote:

- Compliance administrator
- Compliance data administrator
- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admin
- Security administrator

claims.claim: Fabric DLP does not support other policy templates; administrators must choose Custom and Custom policy.
claims.quote:
Choose the Custom category and then the Custom policy template. When done, select Next.
... No other categories or templates are currently supported.

claims.claim: Administrative units are unsupported for Fabric DLP.
claims.quote: Admin units are not supported for DLP in Fabric and Power BI.

claims.claim: Restrict access is configured inside a policy rule, while the policy location determines the workspaces covered.
claims.quote: After you've enabled Fabric and Power BI as the DLP location for the policy and chosen which workspaces the policy will apply to, select Next.

claims.claim: The two cmdlet reference pages do not name Fabric lakehouses or semantic models.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Fabric DLP restrict access PowerShell New-DlpComplianceRule BlockAccess PowerBIDlpLocation'; searched the fetched New-DlpComplianceRule and New-DlpCompliancePolicy references for Fabric, lakehouse and semantic. No such item names appeared.

claims.claim: The Purview Alerts page provides monitoring of Fabric DLP matches.
claims.quote: If you enable alerts in the policy, an alert records on the data loss prevention Alerts page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Activity explorer can display Fabric DLP data.
claims.quote: You can view data from DLP for Fabric and Power BI in Activity explorer.

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically explain whether lakehouse changes made by service principals receive the same exception as semantic models.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Fabric lakehouse DLP service principal evaluation restrict access'; read the overview and troubleshoot-restricted-access. The exception names semantic models; the troubleshooting SPN example names mirrored databases, not lakehouses.
